title: Diet/exercise counseling = health promotion (primary prevention)
vignette: A 28-year-old woman comes to the office to establish care. She recently moved to New York to begin a job as a copy editor at a major newspaper. She has no known medical problems. The patient usually eats fast food for lunch, and she and her husband cook in the evenings. She goes to the gym about once every 2 weeks. The patient's temperature is 36.7 C (98 F), blood pressure is 118/64 mm Hg, pulse is 60/min, and respirations are 14/min. Her BMI is 24.6 kg/m2. Physical examination is unremarkable. Laboratory results are within the normal range. Counseling this patient regarding diet and exercise habits would be an example of which of the following?

clues.text: She has no known medical problems
clues.note: The patient is healthy with normal labs - so counseling aims to PREVENT disease from developing (primary prevention), not to detect or treat it.

clues.text: Counseling this patient regarding diet and exercise habits
clues.note: Advising healthy diet and exercise to a well person is HEALTH PROMOTION - improving determinants of health to prevent disease onset (primary prevention).

whatMatters: Counseling a HEALTHY patient about diet and exercise to prevent future disease is HEALTH PROMOTION - a form of PRIMARY prevention (preventing a disease process from ever becoming established). Answer D.
strategy: Classify by prevention level. PRIMARY = prevent disease onset (health promotion, immunization, no smoking, exercise). SECONDARY = detect asymptomatic disease early (screening, case finding). TERTIARY = limit complications of established disease (rehab, BP/glucose control). Diet/exercise counseling in a well person = health promotion (primary). Reject case finding/health risk assessment (secondary), tertiary prevention (established disease), community-level intervention (population policy), and CBT/precontemplative-stage intervention (behavior-change therapy specifics).

eliminations.label: Case finding - secondary prevention (screening)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: looking for asymptomatic disease in patients already receiving care (a form of SECONDARY prevention). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it detects existing (asymptomatic) disease, whereas counseling here aims to PREVENT disease (primary). ✅ Correct if: age/gender-appropriate screening for occult disease.

eliminations.label: Cognitive-behavioral therapy - a psychotherapy modality
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a structured psychotherapy targeting maladaptive thoughts (for mental illness). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is a treatment technique, not the prevention category for diet/exercise counseling. ✅ Correct if: treating anxiety/depression/eating disorders.

eliminations.label: Community-level intervention - population policy
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: population measures (e.g., soda taxes, smoke-free laws). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this is INDIVIDUAL counseling, not a community-wide intervention. ✅ Correct if: a public-health policy at the community level.

eliminations.label: Health risk assessment - questionnaire-based risk age
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a tool that computes a patient's 'risk age' from demographic/lifestyle/family data. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it assesses risk rather than being the health-promotion counseling itself. ✅ Correct if: calculating a risk profile/risk age.

eliminations.label: Precontemplative stage intervention - stages of change
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: an intervention for a patient not yet willing to consider change (transtheoretical model). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: nothing indicates she is precontemplative; the question asks the prevention CATEGORY of the counseling. ✅ Correct if: tailoring to a patient's readiness-to-change stage.

eliminations.label: Tertiary prevention - established disease
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: reducing complications/disability of an EXISTING disease (e.g., rehab, glycemic control). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this patient has no disease; the counseling prevents disease onset (primary). ✅ Correct if: managing complications of established disease.

reasoning: Patient is healthy with normal labs; counseling aims to prevent disease from developing
Improving diet and exercise to prevent disease onset is HEALTH PROMOTION
Health promotion falls under PRIMARY prevention
mechanism: Prevention is classified by when it acts relative to disease. PRIMARY prevention keeps a disease process from ever becoming established - it includes HEALTH PROMOTION (per the WHO, 'enabling people to increase control over their health and its determinants') such as encouraging a healthy diet, regular exercise, weight management, and smoking cessation, as well as immunizations. SECONDARY prevention interrupts disease before symptoms appear by detecting it early - e.g., screening and 'case finding' (looking for asymptomatic disease in patients already in care). TERTIARY prevention treats established disease to minimize progression, complications, and disability (e.g., controlling blood pressure/glucose in diabetes, rehabilitation after a stroke). Counseling this healthy woman about diet and exercise is aimed at PREVENTING disease from developing, which is health promotion (primary prevention). The distractors are either different prevention levels (case finding/health risk assessment = secondary; tertiary prevention), population-level rather than individual measures (community intervention), or specific behavior-change constructs/therapies (CBT, precontemplative-stage/stages-of-change intervention) rather than the prevention category.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Biostat/Public Health > prevention levels: primary (health promotion, vaccination - prevent onset), secondary (screening/case finding - detect early), tertiary (limit complications of established disease).

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Counseling a well person on diet/exercise = health promotion = primary prevention.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on primary/secondary/tertiary prevention, health promotion, case finding, or screening? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Case finding/health risk assessment = secondary; tertiary = established disease; community intervention = population; CBT/stages-of-change = therapy constructs.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: primary prevention = health promotion + vaccination; secondary = screening/case finding; tertiary = limit complications.
